statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail sits in the lower watch band while Stress stays elevated on the multi-decade-high long end.
recommendation: Structure remains two-way: Thursday's opening gap was fully retraced before the index faded back below the prior close. Stress stays elevated because the 30-year Treasury yield is at a 2004 high and crude is up close to 3%. The US power hour into the 20:00Z cash close is flagged as the narrow danger window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 fades off its gap-fill high as the global bond selloff deepens; Tail in the watch band
body: NDX opened at 30,225.19 against a 30,470.29 prior close, set the session low at 30,204.16, then fully retraced the gap and printed 30,529.35 above the prior close before easing to 30,437.92, down 0.11%, at the assessment cutoff. The 325-point range has been traded in both directions with completed retracements, so mean reversion is functioning. VIX is 15.74 against a 15.18 prior close, off its 16.57 high but back up from the 15.34 low, which is why Tail is placed in the lower watch band rather than the low band. The macro backdrop is hostile and bear-steepening: the 30-year Treasury yield is near 5.46%, its highest since 2004, and the 10-year near 5.165%, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year is unchanged at about 4.90% - a term-premium and inflation move rather than a pure Fed-path repricing. The 30-year mortgage rate printed 7.03% today, the first reading above 7% since early 2025. WTI rose 2.75% to about $94.69 and Brent 3.11% to about $106.29, though both came off their peaks on reports that US and Iranian negotiators in New York are discussing a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, so the oil impulse is conflicting rather than aligned. Thursday's US data was firm: initial jobless claims 197K and new home sales 0.684M, both better than consensus. Oracle's force majeure notice on its Project Jupiter data centre pressured the AI-infrastructure complex, and index internals are split rather than one-way, with META up 3.6% against MSFT down 1.0% and AVGO down 1.4%, and semiconductors averaging -0.84% on wide dispersion. Conflicting cross-asset signals alongside observed two-way NQ structure keep Tail in the watch band while Stress stays elevated. Shared Finviz context collected at 17:35Z was within the 90-minute freshness window but partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor figures were used only as non-real-time confirmation evidence, and all price levels quoted here come from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours stayed inside a persistent watch band. Tail ran at 20-24 through Wednesday's late US afternoon and evening, eased to 17-19 across the Asian overnight as conditions normalised, then rebuilt to a 25 peak at 09:00 UTC on a trend-down European session driven by the bond selloff. It has since oscillated between 19 and 24 with a mixed dominant mode, and the most recent published hour read 19. Stress held between 49 and 58 throughout and Confidence between 85 and 88, describing a difficult but consistently mean-reverting environment rather than a pathological one-way path.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-way trade inside Thursday's 30,204-30,529 range, with conditional Tail lifted to the top of the watch band only for the 19:00-20:15 UTC power hour and cash close, where late repositioning against multi-decade-high yields is most plausible. Conditional Tail then eases through the post-close and Asian overnight to the mid-teens absent a fresh catalyst, before rebuilding through the European morning and the 09:15 UTC Fed Williams speech. The highest conditional-risk pairing of the forecast is Friday's 12:30 UTC durable goods release and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, because opening-auction continuation after a data surprise is the pattern most capable of denying retracement; that window is a scheduled checkpoint, not observed structure, and conditional Tail is deliberately held below the blocking threshold there. The reading would be understated if NQ were to hold near a session extreme on shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements; it would ease further if long-end yields stabilise, the Hormuz negotiations progress and volatility resumes decaying.

forecastDetail.comment: Opening gap from 30,470 down to 30,225 was fully retraced with a 30,529 print above the prior close, and the index has since eased to 30,438 with VIX at 15.74; two-way structure is intact.
Power hour into the 20:00Z close is the narrowest conditional window: late repositioning against a 2004-high long end could extend the fade, invalidated by a hold inside the 30,204-30,529 range.
Cash close and settlement can carry a closing imbalance past the bell, but that push normally stalls as volume drops; a close back inside the session range would confirm mean reversion held.
Post-close futures have no scheduled catalyst and conditional Tail returns to the low band; an unscheduled US-Iran Hormuz headline remains the residual route to an oil-driven move.
Thin evening futures with no catalyst mark the quiet part of the forecast; Stress stays higher than Tail because thin books can exaggerate any unscheduled headline.
